The patch removes the line that updates minValue, which breaks the algorithm's logic for finding the most negative coefficient. It only passes the test by accident because it finds the first negative value instead of the most negative one, which happens to work for this specific test case but violates the documented contract and will fail on other inputs.

The patch removes the line that updates minValue, which breaks the algorithm's logic for finding the most negative coefficient. By not updating minValue, the comparison always uses 0 as the threshold, causing it to select the first negative value rather than the most negative one. This is a fundamental algorithmic error that only passes the specific test case by accident.
